title: The ten days
hook: the days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are for making amends

segments.voice: Yesterday, the three books, and the middle one still open. Your line was write us in. Today, the days when that middle book is being written.

There's a particular feeling to the days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. The holiday food is in the fridge. Work and school have started again. Life looks ordinary, but people who keep these days describe a hum underneath, like the week before a big exam. Words in the daily prayers shift. Someone you haven't heard from in a year calls, a bit awkwardly, to say they're sorry.
screen: `LIFE LOOKS ORDINARY.` → `A HUM UNDERNEATH.` → `AN AWKWARD PHONE CALL.`

segments.voice: These are the aseret yemei teshuvah, the ten days of return, counting Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur themselves. The Talmud, in Rosh Hashanah 18a, reads a verse from Isaiah as being about these days: "Seek ye the LORD while He may be found, call ye upon Him while He is near." These are the near days. The daily Amidah changes to match. All year, one blessing ends: the holy God. For these ten days it ends: the holy King. Forget, and in many traditions you go back and say it again. Avinu Malkeinu, our father, our king, is said at many services, and some people take on stricter habits just for these days. At the center is teshuvah, usually translated repentance, though the word means return, turning back. Maimonides lays out what it involves. You recognize what you did wrong. You regret it. You say it out loud, in words, to God. And you resolve not to do it again. Then he gives a test for whether teshuvah is complete. You find yourself in the same situation, with the same temptation, the same person, the same chance, and this time you choose differently. Not because you can't. Because you've changed. That's the work of these days: not grand gestures but specific turns, one person, one habit, one sentence. Ten days is not long. Long enough to do something, short enough that it can't be put off.
screen: `TEN DAYS OF RETURN.` · `SEEK WHILE HE IS NEAR.` · `THE HOLY GOD BECOMES THE HOLY KING.` · `SAME SITUATION, NEW CHOICE.` · then, large: `TEN DAYS TO TURN.`

segments.voice: Let a face come to mind, someone you hurt this year in a big way or a small one, and walk quietly through Maimonides' steps: what did I do, do I regret it, can I say it in words, what would I do differently? Then find the first sentence of an apology, the actual words you'd say or text, simple and specific. If you pray, you can bring it to God as well.
Teshuvah. Return: recognizing what you did wrong, regretting it, saying so, and resolving to choose differently, the work of these ten days of return.
Your line: ten days to turn. Not a grand gesture, a specific turn. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: During the Ten Days of Repentance, Jews change wording in the Amidah (HaMelech HaKadosh), say Avinu Malkeinu, add selichot, and many seek out people they have wronged to apologize before Yom Kippur.
